questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Makes a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Protects you if you crash.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket made of leather when riding. Leather protects you in a crash. In hot weather, leather jackets help protect you from dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to the frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: You can be easier to see by wearing bright, reflective clothing. Always ride with your headlight on and use your turn signals and brake light.

questions.question: To get the most protection, choose a helmet that:

options.text: Fits loosely.
Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Has survived a previous crash.
Provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: Keep adequate space between you and the vehicle ahead so you can:

options.text: Have time and space to spot and react to hazards.
Tailgate safely.
Allow traffic counters to count you as a vehicle.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space between you and the car ahead gives you room to stop or swerve if they stop suddenly. It also helps you see hazards on the road, like potholes.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is okay if you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is okay if no other vehicles are nearby.
Can move you into another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can move you into another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could end up in another lane or off the road. Use caution when turning.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: The most effective way to survive a crash is to wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, be ready for:

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you the most space between your motorcycle and any hazards.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may need to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: The driver cannot see you if you ride in their blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape path if danger appears.

questions.question: The correct body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Has you sitting forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
Has you sitting as far back as possible and stretching to reach the grips.
Has you leaning over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keeps your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has you sitting forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when you hold the grips. This lets you easily reach and use the controls.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have been drinking. Do whatever you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: What can you do in a no passing zone on a motorcycle?

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones prohibit all passing. You cannot pass by leaving the main road either.

questions.question: What footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that support your ankles give the best protection. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in before riding.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually does not change how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It is encouraged to help new riders learn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a riding group small?

options.text: A small group is less likely to get separated in traffic.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always try to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to know where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is less likely to get separated in traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to get separated by traffic or lights, and do not pressure slower riders to hurry.

questions.question: What material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: On what surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?

options.text: Dry pavement
Gravel
Snow
Leaves

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal covers all reduce traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface for motorcycles.

questions.question: Why is proper clothing important when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothing should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Clothing does not need to cover your arms or legs.
You do not need a jacket in warm weather.
Clothing can protect you in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing can protect you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly but not restrict your movement.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent mechanical problems. Small issues on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: What can happen from long-term wind noise exposure while riding?

options.text: It is recommended.
It can cause hearing loss.
It is not harmful.
It is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to estimate pressure.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire by hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A visual check is not reliable because an under-inflated tire may still look normal.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet roads, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement provides the best grip.

questions.question: What can help other drivers see your motorcycle at an intersection?

options.text: Use your headlight while riding.
Swerve within your lane to get attention.
Raise your arms.
Avoid using your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight while riding.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight at intersections. Position your motorcycle in the lane so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of crashing?

options.text: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Ride in spots where others cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by staying visible. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show other drivers what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders check over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle.
It gets the attention of other drivers.
Mirrors do not work well.
You should make eye contact with nearby drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How does your body get rid of alcohol?

options.text: Time.
Drinking coffee.
Exercising.
Taking a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.
